summary: Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche.
Trịnh Xuân Thuận studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1970) and Princeton University (~1970–1974). He held a post at the University of Virginia around 1976.

Tse-fu Kuan completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich in 2004. A Buddhist studies scholar, he conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned a Geshe Lharampa at Ganden Monastery and held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery. He taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Alexander Berzin, Joseph Loizzo, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow. Working in Tibetology and linguistics, he served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and became Instructor in Tibetan at the University of Oxford in 2001.
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Tsering Gyaltsen studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under the traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya studied at SOAS University of London (BA ~1978–1981, MPhil 2000, PhD ~2000–2004). A specialist in Tibetology and history, he held posts at SOAS (1999–2002), the University of Oxford, and the University of British Columbia (~2005).
Tsewang Gyurme, active in Tibetology and history, served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche (1953–2020), a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Khampagar Monastery (~1979–1990) and under several teachers, including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima. He founded the Pundarika Foundation and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsu-lin Mei (1933–2023) was a scholar of linguistics and sinology. He studied at Oberlin College, Harvard University, and Yale University, later holding posts at Harvard (~1964–1971) and Cornell University (~1971–2000).

Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University Bloomington under Christopher I. Beckwith and others. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019), a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology, studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as president of Reiyukai and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and founded the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo in the field of Buddhist studies.

Tsukasa Mizushima studied at the University of Tokyo (graduating ~1976, MA ~1979, PhD 1992). A historian and indologist, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and the University of Tokyo (1997–2018), and chaired the Historical Society of Japan.

Tsultrim Allione, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earned a master's degree at Antioch University and studied under traditional teachers including Chögyam Trungpa and the 16th Karmapa. She founded Tara Mandala in 1993.
Tsultrim Gyatso, working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002) at Otani University, and was a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki, working in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1963–1967). He held posts at Doshisha University (~1974–1992) and Kyoto University (~1992–2007), serving as professor at Kyoto.

Tsuruji Sahoda (1899–1986), a scholar of indology and philosophy, studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He later held academic posts at Osaka University (~1949–1963) and Ritsumeikan University (~1963–1970).
